A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LaVin-DiT work, with matching core methods and experiments. Text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. v1 ends with references; v4 additionally contains readable supplementary Sections A–D and Figures 8–30.

before.justification: v1 reports original multitask benchmark results in Tables 1–2, qualitative predictions in Figure 3, and scaling, latency, and context-length experiments in Figures 4–7.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds extensive qualitative predictions and a single-view scene-reconstruction demonstration in its supplement.

M1.justification: The ST-VAE, joint diffusion transformer, attention mechanisms, 3D RoPE, flow-matching objective, and inference procedure remain unchanged. Appendix A supplies mathematical detail and pseudocode for existing components; it does not establish a revised model or algorithm.

E1.justification: The existing image/video training coverage and quantitative benchmarks are retained. Figure 30 adds an actual single-view scene-reconstruction demonstration using predicted depth. Most supplementary galleries elaborate existing tasks, including pose-to-image generation already illustrated in v1 Figure 3. The text-conditioned applications mentioned in Appendix D are not evaluated.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains MAE, MAE-VQGAN, and LVM; Table 2 retains DPT, StableNormal, Marigold, and LVM in the same comparisons. The latency comparison still uses LVM. The added qualitative galleries introduce no comparator methods.

E3.justification: Appendix B.2 reports 1,000 ImageNet validation images for inpainting, whereas v1 Section 4.2 specifies 2,500. v4 also retains the 2,500 statement, creating a limited inconsistency in the reported protocol rather than establishing a rerun. The main training budgets and evaluation settings otherwise remain unchanged; most supplementary settings are newly disclosed details.

E4.justification: The scaling, latency, and context-length analyses in Figures 4–7 are unchanged. Figure 30 adds a concrete application case study showing how predicted depth supports reconstruction and alternative scene views. The broader qualitative galleries do not introduce controlled component ablations or robustness tests.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures for the benchmark results. The supplement introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice, and the original plots remain identical.

E6.justification: Figures 8–29 substantially expand the qualitative result record across 22 image/video tasks, including additional optical-flow and conditional-video-generation predictions; Figure 30 adds reconstructed scene views. Existing quantitative results remain identical, including depth AbsRel 6.2 and inpainting FID 1.65 in Table 2. The expansion concerns qualitative evidence, with no demonstrated quantitative performance change.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 adds block-rotation definitions and a derivation of the relative-position attention property for 3D RoPE, through Equations (4)–(10). This is a limited mathematical addition around an existing component; the main flow-matching equations are unchanged. The added Equation (7) reverses the relative-position sign implied by the rotation convention in Equation (5).

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: unified image/video processing, adaptation through visual context without fine-tuning, scalability, and strong performance and efficiency. The changed code/model availability statement concerns access rather than a new scientific contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix D broadens the applicability discussion to text-to-image/video generation, visual editing, robotics, and autonomous driving, including assertions of adaptation without supervised fine-tuning. These uses receive little direct support beyond the reconstruction demonstration. The original explanations of scaling and context-length effects, and limitations concerning out-of-distribution tasks and resources, remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Algorithms 1–2, Table 3, Table 4, and Appendix B add substantial reproducibility information: timestep sampling, model widths/layers/heads, latent channels, EMA and clipping settings, dataset splits and counts, annotation-generation tools, and evaluation preprocessing. These largely document the retained system. v4 also replaces a promised code/model release with stated availability and a project link.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations including DEEM, Diception, a multitask dense-prediction survey, and sources for depth and Pascal-5i evaluation. The related-work prose and positioning around image-resembling generation, sequential modeling, diffusion transformers, and visual in-context learning remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order remain nearly verbatim. v4 adds organized supplementary Sections A–D, updates the availability sentence, and corrects the scalability passage's reference from 'Table 5' to 'Figure 5'. There is little rewriting of the existing exposition.

P2.justification: v4 adds extensive task-specific visual galleries and a reconstruction display in Figures 8–30, two detailed supplementary tables, and two algorithm blocks. It also repositions the original Tables 1–2 and Figure 3. The original plotted data and qualitative Figure 3 content are preserved.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the model configurations, dataset composition, evaluation details, and expanded qualitative examples make the work easier to inspect and reproduce. These provide a net improvement in transparency. The benefit is limited by conflicting inpainting sample counts, the sign error in the added RoPE derivation, and unsupported extensions of the applicability discussion. The original quantitative evidence remains unchanged.
